title: Atypical heart attack, woman 67 ('just the flu')

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Hi, um, I'm calling about my mother. I'm not sure if this is an emergency, maybe I should call 1177 instead.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: That's okay, tell me what's going on.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She's 67, she's been feeling really sick since this morning, she threw up twice. We thought it's the stomach flu.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: At her flat, Södra Esplanaden 9 in Lund.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Is she awake? Is she breathing normally?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She's awake, she's lying on the bed. She's a bit out of breath when she walks to the toilet.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: Not really in the stomach. She says her jaw hurts, kind of up into the teeth, and between the shoulder blades. She thought she slept wrong.

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She's very tired, she's never like this. And she's a bit cold and clammy when I touch her.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: Does she have diabetes or any heart disease?

transcript.speaker: caller
transcript.text: She has diabetes, type 2. She takes metformin.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: I'm sending an ambulance now. Keep her resting, don't let her walk around. If she has aspirin and is not allergic she can chew one.

transcript.speaker: operator
transcript.text: These symptoms can come from the heart, especially in women with diabetes, so we want her checked right away.
